video_specification.overview:
Produce a {DURATION_SECONDS}-second {TONE} video about {TOPIC}. The final deliverable is a rendered MP4 at 1920x1080 30fps generated by Remotion, with continuous narration synthesized via ElevenLabs.
Visual approach: {VISUAL_STYLE}. Every frame has continuous motion. Content fills the frame — no small-icon-in-dark-void compositions. No on-screen text mirrors the voiceover.

prerequisites.environment_setup: - ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is exported in the shell environment - ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID optionally overrides the default voice (Rachel) - Node 20+ and pnpm are available - The Remotion project is pre-scaffolded by the harness driver. It includes @remotion/shapes and @remotion/google-fonts. - public/assets/ may contain Wikipedia-sourced reference images (see assets.json in the project root). - Do not touch package.json dependencies.

technology_stack.audio_format: MP3 from ElevenLabs, served from public/audio.mp3
technology_stack.captions: NONE — there are no on-screen captions or subtitles
technology_stack.assets: Wikipedia-sourced images in public/assets/ via the Phase Assets step (catalog in assets.json)

video_specification.narrative_arc:
{NARRATIVE_ARC_PROSE}
Three to five sentences describing what the audience learns and in what order. Phase A (downstream) reads this to write narration and decide phrase cuts. Do NOT write the literal voiceover here.

visual_style.frame_fill_rule: Every shot's rendered content must occupy at least 60% of the frame's pixels. A small icon centered in a dark void is not a shot. If your visual is small, expand it, add supporting elements, tile it, or zoom in until it fills the frame.
visual_style.forbidden: - No on-screen text mirroring the voiceover - No static frames - No small centered icon in a flat dark void (the default "text-on-background" anti-pattern) - No repeating the same composition across adjacent shots

pacing_rules.rule: Every frame has continuous motion. Static frames are forbidden.
Phrase rhythm drives shot boundaries — a statement is a shot, a connecting clause is a transition, a punchy single word can be its own shot. Phase A makes these calls.
Shot complexity (simple/complex/transition) is derived from each shot's duration after TTS; shot agents use it as a visual density hint.
No two adjacent shots may use the same composition layout.

step.title: Phase A — Director
step.tasks: - Read video_spec.xml - Write script.json: continuous narration + phrases (role: shot | transition) + optional anchors - Stop

step.title: Phase Assets — Wikipedia image fetcher
step.tasks: - Asset scout agent reads script + spec, writes asset_search_terms.json - Driver hits Wikipedia REST API, downloads images to public/assets/ - Produces assets.json catalog

step.title: TTS
step.tasks: - Driver synthesizes narration via ElevenLabs, derives shot frame ranges from phrases

step.title: Phase B — Shot components (parallel, max 5 concurrent)
step.tasks: - One shot agent per timing.shots[i] - Each writes src/shots/Shot{NN}.tsx + Shot{NN}.anchors.json - Uses palette, typography, assets from spec + assets.json - Obeys frame-fill rule and composition catalog

step.title: Phase C — Compositor
step.tasks: - Assemble src/Root.tsx with Audio + shot Sequences (no captions) - Run vitest alignment test, render to out/video.mp4

success_criteria.functionality: - alignment.test.ts passes - out/video.mp4 exists - No on-screen text mirrors the voiceover - No static frames - Content fills the frame in every shot (≥60% pixels) - Adjacent shots use different compositional layouts - The palette is topic-specific (not the generic Claude dark + orange)
